Marissa / Monica —

Quick notes I drafted to feed the questionnaire and for the call with Alice: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood Inference completed SOC 2 Type II (Security and Availability) for our hosted API in Q2 2026. We can provide a redacted PDF of the SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA (PII removed). Full report is available under standard non-disclosure and controlled access.

2) Subprocessors / Cloud providers: primary compute and storage for the hosted offering is on AWS (us-west-2 and us-east-1), with optional GCP regions for customers with GCP requirements. Key subprocessors include: AWS (EC2, S3), HashiCorp (Vault for secrets management), Datadog (monitoring), Sentry (error reporting), and Postgres (managed DB). We keep a canonical subprocessor spreadsheet with service, purpose, and data access scope — please attach that to the vendor response.

3) GDPR: we support regional processing and have contractual data processing terms. For EU customers we can provision EU-only processing and storage; we also provide standard DPAs.

4) HIPAA / BAA: Redwood will sign a BAA for customers ingesting PHI. Dedicated or Private deployment is recommended for PHI workloads; Hosted customers can be covered under BAA with appropriate controls and limited support access.

5) Embeddings / Derived data: embeddings derived from customer inputs are treated as customer data. By default, they are stored and processed within the tenant environment; access is limited to automated runtime services and authorized operations engineers under strict access controls and audit logging. We do not use customer content to train our models.

6) Attachments to include: redacted_soc2_type2_2026.pdf and subprocessor_list_20261120.xlsx. Vivek will take point on the technical Qs (network segmentation, key management, KV cache handling).

I can join the follow-up call — propose we offer 30m on Wed 11/25 at 10am PT (confirm availability).

-Aditya

Hi Alice —

Thanks — attaching the redacted SOC 2 report and the current subprocessor list. Aditya / Vivek answered the high-level questions below; I’ve also filled the non-technical sections of your questionnaire and attached a working copy.

Answers to your specific follow-ups: 
- Retention windows: default request logs = 90 days, embeddings = 365 days (configurable), KV cache = ephemeral per session (configurable per deployment). We can support shorter retention windows for regulated datasets in Dedicated/Private deployments and via contractual DPA controls.
- Support access: access is granted through our internal access workflow — engineers request time-limited access via Jira + SSO just-in-time provisioning; all access is logged and archived for audits.
- Subprocessors and access to plaintext: subprocessors do not have routine access to plaintext customer content. Backups and logs are encrypted at rest; where subprocessors process telemetry/metrics (e.g., Datadog), data is aggregated and does not contain unredacted customer content. Any exceptions are noted in the subprocessor spreadsheet.

Next steps: 
1) Attached: redacted_soc2_type2_2026.pdf, subprocessor_list_20261120.xlsx, vendor_questionnaire_filled_20261123.pdf
2) We’ll target completing any remaining technical Qs by end of day Tuesday (2026-11-24).
3) Proposed follow-up call with Aditya/Vivek: Wed 11/25 at 10am PT — please confirm availability.

If you’d like, we can also put together a short security pack (SOC 2 summary, DPA template, BAA summary) for your legal/procurement team.

Best,
